title.narrative: Provision of life-saving WASH Assistance for IDPs and Host Communities in Ar-Raqqa and Al-Hasakeh Governorates, Northeast Syria

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis project proposes a time-sensitive WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) intervention to sustain essential sanitation and hygiene services and prevent public health deterioration in Ar-Raqqa and Al-Hasakeh governorates, specifically in the sub-districts of Ar-Raqqa, Ath Thawrah, Quamishli, and Kasab (Al-Hasakeh city). The intervention targets internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and vulnerable host communities focusing on emergency collective centers, while extending some activities to IDP camps, informal settlements and underserved areas. ltbrgtFollowing the sudden withdrawal of institutional donor funding, INGOs face an urgent gap in its ability to continue delivering sanitation and hygiene services in these locations. Without immediate support, over 60,000 individuals—already living in crisis-affected conditions—face increased risk of disease outbreaks and deepening WASH-related vulnerabilities. ltbrgtActivities are aligned with the Syria Humanitarian Fund priorities and include: ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtSanitation response, including desludging, distribution of latrine cleaning sets, routine latrine maintenance, minor repairs, and installation of safety measures to ensure the continued functionality of critical facilities and ensure safe and dignified access lt/ligtltligtEmergency solid-waste management, through four community cleaning campaigns, partnerships with waste collection service providers, and provision of safety equipment, while supporting local authorities lt/ligtltligtAccess to emergency essential NFIs, through the distribution of Hygiene Refill kits (including menstrual hygiene items), prioritizing women, girls, and persons with disabilities, with contents tailored to address dignity, privacy, and health lt/ligtltligtCommunity-based hygiene promotion, delivered alongside kits by trained male and female facilitators using context-sensitive approaches adapted for different age groups and literacy levels, and focusing on best practices to reduce disease transmission and increase environmental awareness. lt/ligtltligtWater supply is not included in this intervention, as it is currently being covered by other WASH actors in the targeted areas. CARE’s response will complement these existing efforts by sustaining parallel hygiene and sanitation components at risk of collapse due to the funding shortfall. lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtCARE has an established operational presence and trusted relationships with local stakeholders across the targeted sub-districts. While the main beneficiaries will be IDPs, certain activities, such as the distribution of essential NFIs, will also extend to IDP camps, informal settlements, and vulnerable host community members, using an emergency gap-filling approach. Furthermore, returnees in these areas will benefit from essential NFIs, hygiene promotion campaigns, and the maintenance of WASH facilities. To ensure a comprehensive and inclusive approach, CARE will implement a blanket targeting strategy within the collective centers, ensuring that all individuals in need are reached. Activities will be coordinated with the Sub-National WASH Cluster and the targeting will be coordinated with other partners with ongoing initiatives in the area to avoid duplication of efforts and maximize impact. ltbrgtThe project applies a strong gender, age, and disability lens, recognizing that women, girls, older persons, and individuals with disabilities often face heightened WASH-related risks. ltbrgtThe project embeds accountability and community engagement mechanisms throughout. CARE will maintain accessible, confidential, and inclusive complaints and feedback systems, ensuring affected populations—including illiterate persons and those with specific needs—can provide input and influence programming decisions. ltbrgtBy sustaining sanitation and hygiene service delivery, this intervention will mitigate disease risks, uphold public health standards, and protect vulnerable populations amid worsening economic conditions, ongoing displacement, and operational uncertainty in Northeast Syria. lt/pgt
